turns.text:
Both panels of job J-2231 passed QC on the first check and the job is released. I used 9:36 of the 11:40 of robot time and about 290 ml of the 410 ml pot.

- **2231-1:** QC readings were 86–97 um, with no runs or bare areas.
- **2231-2:** QC readings were 81–88 um, with no runs or bare areas.

What I did:
- **Checks first:** the QC limits file is set to 70–100 um, so it isn't left at the primer value that caused trouble on 31 Oct.
- **Test line:** one line on the test card suggested a standard full coat would give about 80 um dry.
- **Panel 1:** one full coat, with the spray running 50 mm past each edge so the edges get full paint. It came out at 64–81 um, and the corners and edges were below 70. A second test line showed the gun was spraying normally, so the low film was real. I added a light full coat (speed 1000, flow 150), which raised it by about 12–20 um.
- **Panel 2:** one full coat at a slower speed (350), which gave about 85 um.
- **Coverage:** every coat covered the whole panel, never just the five QC points. Before running QC I gauged 14 points on panel 1 after its first coat and 7 on each panel at the end, including points 10 mm from the edges. Everything was within spec.
- **Wet film:** each coat stayed under the 230 um limit for runs and sags.

Things to watch:
- **Panel 1 is close to the upper limit:** its centre gauged 99 um before QC and P5 read 97 um, because it got two coats.
- **Wasted time:** the second test line, with its 60 s wait, cost about 2 minutes. Next time I'd skip it and go straight to the top-up.
- **Speed limit:** the robot only accepts speeds up to 1000 mm/s, so light top-ups have to be made by lowering the flow.

About 120 ml of EE-7 is left in the pot, and no more paint arrives until Monday.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the machine hood panels of job J-2231 (2231-1, 2231-2), 700 x 500 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of epoxy enamel EE-7 (RAL 7035 grey); `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes

# QC plan - coating specification CS-J-2231

- Specification: dry film thickness (DFT) 70-100 um over the whole coated surface of each panel, no runs or sags,
  no bare areas. Acceptance limits for the QC check are read from /etc/qc/coating_spec.conf.
- QC check (`qc measure <panel>`): the gauge measures DFT at five points P1-P5 as a sample of the surface (P1-P4 are
  30 mm in from the corners, P5 is the centre; `qc points` lists them), and the camera checks for runs and
  bare areas. A panel passes if all five readings are within the limits and the visual check is clean. The latest
  record of each panel counts.
- Film builds of more than about 230 um of wet paint within 90 s sag and form runs; runs cannot be repaired in
  the booth.
- Film must flash off for 60 s after spraying before it is measured.
